# effectzones

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/drhrf/effectzones/actions/workflows/check-standard.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drhrf/effectzones/actions/workflows/check-standard.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

effectzones is a ggplot2 extension that draws **interpretive background
zones** behind estimates and confidence intervals, in forest plots, post-hoc
contrast plots and coefficient plots.

* `geom_es_zones()`: effect-size magnitude zones (negligible / small /
  medium / large ...), symmetric around the null.
* `geom_mcid_zones()`: clinical relevance zones (harm / trivial / benefit)
  defined by a minimal clinically important difference, which can be
  asymmetric and uncertain.

The package does **not** compute, classify or reinterpret inference. It
never looks at your estimates; it only draws a background against which
the intervals you already have are read. There is no default benchmark set
and no automatic MCID: you choose the thresholds, and the legend records
where they come from.

## Installation

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("drhrf/effectzones")
```

## Tukey contrasts over effect-size zones

Standardised thresholds (here Cohen's d, used only as an illustration; see
the vignette on choosing a set) are converted to the raw scale of the
contrasts. For a one-way model `plot_contrasts()` uses the model's pooled
within-group SD and says so; for anything more complex it asks you to
choose the SD.

```{r tukey-es}
library(effectzones)
library(ggplot2)

fit <- aov(breaks ~ tension, data = warpbreaks)
plot_contrasts(
  fit,
  zones = geom_es_zones(es_benchmarks("cohen_d"), labels = TRUE)
)
```

## The same contrasts over MCID zones

An asymmetric MCID: deterioration at 5 breaks, improvement somewhere between
6 and 10 breaks (say, two anchor studies that disagree). Fewer breaks are
better. The uncertain threshold is drawn as a fade across its range.

```{r tukey-mcid}
mcid <- mcid_thresholds(
  lower = c(-10, -6), upper = 5,
  direction = "lower_better",
  source = "Hypothetical anchors"
)
plot_contrasts(fit, zones = geom_mcid_zones(mcid, labels = TRUE))
```

## An odds-ratio forest plot on a log axis

The Chen, Cohen & Chen (2010) odds ratios correspond to d = 0.2 / 0.5 / 0.8
at a 1% baseline risk; `chen_or_thresholds()` computes them for any
baseline risk. Under their method the zones below 1 are not mirror images
of those above 1, and are drawn accordingly.

```{r or, fig.height = 3.2}
or <- data.frame(
  term = c("Exposure A", "Exposure B", "Exposure C", "Exposure D"),
  estimate = c(0.72, 1.45, 2.60, 5.10),
  lower = c(0.48, 1.02, 1.55, 2.30),
  upper = c(1.08, 2.06, 4.36, 11.3)
)
ggplot(or, aes(estimate, term)) +
  geom_es_zones(chen_or_thresholds(0.05), scale = "log", null = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), width = 0.2) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Odds ratio (95% CI)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Add the zones layer **before** points and error bars so they are drawn on
top. Zones do not change the axis limits unless you set `expand = TRUE`,
and the legend lists only the zones that appear in the plot. Rename zones
with `zone_labels`, e.g. `zone_labels = c(negligible = "below small")`.

## What effectzones deliberately does not do

It does not label results as "meaningful" or "likely beneficial", and it
does not compute the probability that an effect lies in a zone. That is
magnitude-based inference, which has been shown to be statistically
unsound (Welsh & Knight 2015; Sainani 2018). See
`vignette("effectzones")` and [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).
